content.text:
The six-item check cannot support independent-competence certification on the supplied evidence. My evidence L-S1 says its items repeat interface examples; they provide neither delayed nor changed-case evidence. Use them as a practice checkpoint to identify difficulties with those examples. Analyst's disclosure that no delayed unassisted assessment exists further limits the readiness claim. L-S2 says an assessor can review two changed-case exercises within this project, and no validated certification instrument is available. Those two exercises can inform subsequent practice; they cannot establish readiness for 220 workers or all shifts.

I advise reserving 2 units for brief practice and 2 for a bounded changed-case check. For two selected workers, propose a 15-minute sequence: five minutes of guided practice, five minutes attempting one unfamiliar exception case without coaching, then five minutes of feedback. The assessor would review exactly those two attempts. Record assistance, the worker's explanation of the decision and escalation, and unresolved difficulties; any operational correctness criteria need Ops' confirmation. This is a proposed time allocation, not demonstrated feasibility. For other workers, brief practice must remain within their 15-minute allowance and actual staffing; I cannot assume the single clinic reaches every shift.

Together with the proposed 2-unit workflow work, 2-unit audit and my single 1-unit consultation fee, this design totals 9 units, leaving 1. The 3-unit paper fallback drill does not fit alongside that package. Ops must decide staffing, selection and operational release. Independent competence, delayed retention and workforce-wide transfer remain unknown; I provide assessment advice, not certification or operational authorization.
